page: UpCloud PREMIUM-48xCPU-96GB is a KVM-hypervised server featuring 48 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The system operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with 48 physical cores and a shared CPU allocation. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 400 GB local SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench metrics. It also achieves top-tier results in software compilation with Clang, single-threaded gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression. Cryptographic and vector execution capabilities are supported by hardware flags including AVX-512, AES, and SHA_NI, contributing to strong performance in Passmark CPU encryption and physics tests. Memory bandwidth is strong, reaching 261.26 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, though Passmark memory scores sit in the average tier.

While the server excels at raw compute-bound tasks and prompt processing for small language models, it exhibits weaker performance in text generation tasks, particularly with small models where it falls into the bottom tier. Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this configuration is highly compute-optimized. It is well-suited for CPU-intensive workloads such as software compilation, image processing, static web serving, and database operations, but less optimal for memory-intensive datasets or large-scale LLM text generation.
